articles.title: Hopwood Hall Volunteer Expresses Disappointment Over High Court Ruling
articles.excerpt: A long-standing volunteer at Hopwood Hall has shared their disappointment regarding the recent High Court ruling affecting the estate, highlighting their deep connection to the site and ongoing restoration efforts.
articles.content_html:

08:26, 02 October 2026

A long-standing volunteer at Hopwood Hall has shared their feelings of disappointment following the recent High Court ruling regarding the estate, emphasising the personal significance of the Hall and its restoration efforts.

A volunteer with over two decades of involvement at Hopwood Hall has expressed disappointment following a recent High Court ruling concerning the estate. The volunteer, who has actively supported the restoration project since 2013, described the Hall as an integral part of their life and community.

In a letter to the editor published by the source, the volunteer recounted their first encounter with Hopwood Hall in 2003, when they discovered the boarded-up building while walking in the surrounding woods. They noted that the Hall, even in its dilapidated state, struck them as a hidden gem worth saving.

The volunteer, along with their brother, became involved in the restoration efforts initiated by Hopwood DePree, who sought to preserve his ancestral home. They participated in the early stages of the project, serving on the original committee and contributing to various restoration activities, including gardening and public engagement during open days. Their efforts were recognised through several awards, reflecting their commitment to the Hall and the community.

The letter highlights the emotional significance of Hopwood Hall to the volunteer and the community, emphasising their dedication to making visitors feel welcome and fostering a positive image of the restoration project. The outcome of the High Court proceedings has raised concerns about the future of the estate and the ongoing efforts to restore it.
